0.x: **Widow remarriage:** the reformer who worked successfully to **legalise widow remarriage**; he **cited the ancient (Vedic) texts** (Parashara) to show widows could remarry → **Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act (Act XV of 1856)**, drafted under **Dalhousie**, **passed under Lord Canning** (July 1856).
**First lawful Hindu widow remarriage:** **Calcutta, 7 December 1856**, under his supervision.

**Women's education:** in 1850 Bethune made him **Secretary of the Hindu Female School**, later the **Bethune School** (founded **1849** by **J.E.D. Bethune**, with Dakshinaranjan Mukherjee); he ran about **35 girls' schools**.
**Principal of the Sanskrit College, Calcutta** (1851) – opened it to non-Brahmins; title "**Vidyasagar**" (Ocean of Learning) for his Sanskrit learning.
**Books:** **Bahubivah (Bahu Bibaho)** against polygamy; Bidhobabivah (widow remarriage); **Barnaparichay** (**Bengali** primer); his prose shaped modern Bengali.
**Somprakash (Som / Shome Prakash), 1858:** Bengali weekly **started on Vidyasagar's plan**, edited by Dwarkanath Vidyabhushan.
**Quote:** "I have no time to think about God; a lot of work has to be done on this earth" – **Vidyasagar**.
**Sambad Kaumudi** (1821) and **Mirat-ul-Akhbar** (1822) were **Rammohan Roy**'s; the 1829 sati ban came from Roy's campaign under **Bentinck**.
**Andhra link:** he sent support for **Veeresalingam's** third widow remarriage.

Malabari** (1853-1912): **Parsi** from Western India (born Baroda), "**greatest Parsi social reformer of the 19th century**"; editor of **Indian Spectator** and **Voice of India**; **Notes on Infant Marriage and Enforced Widowhood (1884)**; **chief crusader for the Age of Consent Act**.
**Tilak opposed** the Bill (Kesari) as foreign interference in Hindu custom; the Moderates (Ranade, Telang, Bhandarkar) supported it.

**Rakhmabai case (1884-88):** married as a child, she refused to live with her husband Dadaji; he sued for **restitution of conjugal rights** – the case raised the **age of consent** and conjugal rights (not women's education); she became one of India's first women doctors.
**Phulmoni Dasi** (1889-90): a child bride's death that pushed the 1891 Act.
The 1891 Act made intercourse with a girl **below 12** an offence, married or not.
